parent.reason: The parent question treats 40 occurrences as one uniform semantic regime, but retrieved evidence shows three materially distinct consequences: (1) non-TDS parameters carry TDS-specific limit-set comment text that does not alter their structured AVG/MAX/MIN comparison; (2) TDS report-only rows (no LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR) are governed by footnote *6/*7 geometric-mean weekly reporting with no numeric limit comparison; (3) TDS net-increase rows with numeric limits use 30-day-average enforcement per permit documents, not geometric-mean weekly reporting. Children supersede the coarse parent; the parent is not independently admissible or independently unresolved.

plan.proposition: What does a geometric-mean reporting comment require for comparison of individual monitoring-period values?
would_establish: Permit footnote *6/*7 text that TDS discharge/intake rows require reporting the geometric mean of weekly values (not a single raw sample) establishes a reporting aggregation rule for TDS report-only limit rows.

Permit statement-of-basis narrative that TDS net incremental increase limits are 30-day averages establishes that numeric TDS net-increase comparisons use AVG/30-day-average semantics, not the geometric-mean weekly reporting instruction.

Identity of the DMR comment text as TDS-specific language propagated at limit-set level to non-TDS parameters establishes that the comment is non-operative for ordinary numeric limit comparison on those rows.

Structured evidence that all 40 rows share one identical comment string while PARAMETER_CODE spans BOD, pH, TSS, E. coli, flow, and TDS would establish limit-set comment carryover rather than a uniform cross-parameter rule.
would_refute: A workspace codebook mapping STATISTICAL_BASE_TYPE_CODE to geometric mean would refute the claim that structured fields leave comparison basis unresolved.
Weekly sub-period sample values in dmr_measurements.csv showing pre-aggregated geometric means would refute the claim that monthly DMR values cannot be verified as geometric means.
Permit text applying footnote *6 geometric-mean reporting to BOD, pH, or other non-TDS parameters would refute the limit-set carryover partition.

Permit text linking the geometric-mean weekly reporting instruction directly to the 497/449 mg/L net-increase limit comparison would refute the reporting-only vs enforcement-statistic split for TDS numeric limits.
insufficient_alone: PRIOR_PACKET.json alone — bounded prior retrieval, not authoritative disposition.
sources/permit_limits.csv alone — shows comment presence and structured AVG/MAX/MIN bases but not permit-authoritative meaning of geometric-mean reporting.
sources/dmr_measurements.csv alone — monthly single values cannot establish whether weekly geometric means were computed or how they relate to limits.

documents/farmington/statement_of_basis.txt E. coli geometric-mean water-quality criteria alone — different parameter context; does not govern TDS footnote *6 or non-TDS limit rows carrying the TDS comment.

candidate_interpretations.description: Individual monitoring-period DMR values must not be compared directly to the limit; compliance requires computing a geometric mean over weekly sub-period samples and comparing that aggregate.

The geometric-mean comment governs how TDS discharge/intake values are reported (geometric mean of weekly values) while numeric net-increase limits use a separate 30-day average enforcement statistic.
The geometric-mean comment is TDS-specific permit language propagated at limit-set level to unrelated parameters; it does not change comparison semantics for non-TDS limits.
As a single parent proposition across all 40 rows, evidence does not support one uniform answer; partitions with different semantic consequences are required.
